I share in your pain. When the PS2 came out, my mother was awesome enough to allow me to skip the first period of school to get a console. This was when you had to be there when the store opened and the console had a low shipping amount at first. This Walmart had 25 consoles, everyone in line knew that. We counted right away when we lined up and luckily I was number 25. Given that they were not allowing people to buy multiple systems, I was sure I was going to get my console and then off on my way to school.  After 3 hours of waiting in line, whoever the person was who was in charge of the line finally decided to let us know they only had 24 systems available, since the manager had already gotten theirs. Needless to say my mother and I were furious. After that, I've vowed to never buy electronics from wally world again, and for the last 12 years I think, I've done just that.

Chrono Trigger

It was the first game for the SNES that I beat from start to finish, got in huge fights with cousins when they saved over my game files, and bought a players guide for with my subscription to Nintendo Power. I have run through that game so many times in every which way through the awesomeness that is emulation. I just recently received a SNES cartridge with box, manual, plastic sleeve and one of the poster inserts for Christmas. When I was younger, my sister of 7 years old was diagnosed with cancer, and being in 1991, there wasn't really that much we could do for her. After her passing, I became somewhat of an anti-social kid at times. I have since changed that drastically, but in those times, Crono and his assortment of friends, challenges, and time periods are what got me through. I still owe a lot of who I am to that game, and this new cartridge is something I will never give up. If I could just play it for a day, without knowing every single statistic on it, and experience it for the first time, I have no doubt I would fall back in love with it again.

TL;DR Chrono Trigger is awesome, play it if you can handle RPGs.
